questions.explain: A single cumulative snapshot hides the signal; the delta between two snapshots 60 seconds apart shows what is actually happening now.
options: Because DMVs reset every 60 seconds
Because absolute values use too many tokens
Because cumulative counters since last restart hide the current signal — deltas reveal it
Because the model cannot read large integers
questions.q: Why should prompt context include wait-stat deltas rather than absolute cumulative values?

questions.explain: Prohibitions convert 'probably won't' into an explicit, testable rule that the Chapter 31 eval harness can verify.
options: To make the prompt sound more authoritative
To reduce token usage in the system prompt
To satisfy compliance documentation requirements
To convert implicit assumptions into explicit, testable rules the eval harness can verify
questions.q: What is the purpose of the PROHIBITIONS section in the triage system prompt?

questions.explain: If every example ends in decisive action, the model learns decisiveness as the pattern; restraint examples teach it to escalate when unsure.
options: To demonstrate the full range of allowed actions
To teach restraint — otherwise the model learns decisiveness as the pattern and becomes trigger-happy
To increase the prompt's token count for better reasoning
To satisfy the JSON schema requirements
questions.q: Why should few-shot examples include cases where the correct output is ALERT_HUMAN or NO_ACTION?

questions.explain: Retry exactly once with a JSON-only nudge, then escalate — scraping prose into executable commands is never acceptable.
options: Retry once with a JSON-only nudge, then escalate to ALERT_HUMAN
Increase temperature and retry until parsing succeeds
Use regex to extract the action and execute it
Discard the incident and log nothing
questions.q: What is the correct handling when a triage model returns invalid JSON?

questions.explain: Separation means a confused diagnosis step cannot directly emit an executable command; planning is a separate, stricter step.
options: It reduces token usage by splitting long prompts
It allows different teams to own each prompt
It prevents a compromised or confused diagnosis step from directly emitting executable commands
It makes the audit log shorter
questions.q: Why separate diagnosis prompts from action-planning prompts instead of using one prompt for the whole workflow?
